note: Strangers: ten side stories across the Sable River country (src/missions/strangers/). Original writing.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: Madam! Stand clear of the road, if you'd be so kind. History is about to come round that bend at eleven miles an hour.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: History's on fire.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: That is the boiler, and it is supposed to... no. No, that isn't supposed to. Madam, the regulator has jammed and my assistant has jumped.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: Catch her! The brake lever is on the left, behind the seat! Do mind the boiler; it bites!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've got the lever! Which way is stop?

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: Toward you! Always toward you! Everything good in engineering is toward you!

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: You've saved the Pettigrew Locomobile, Mark Four, from the fate of Marks One through Three. Two of those are in the Sable. One is in a barn in Ohio, and the barn is in pieces.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Mr. Pettigrew, a horse doesn't explode.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: A horse also doesn't improve, madam. I've watched them for forty years. Not one new idea among them.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: I am raising capital. Twenty dollars buys a share in the Pettigrew Motor Company and the right to say you knew me before the statues.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Twenty dollars. When they put up the statue, see it faces away from the river.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: Madam, you're the first investor who didn't ask for it back before I'd finished the sentence.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've seen what you call stop. I'll keep my money and my eyebrows.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: Everyone says so. Then in ten years they'll all say they knew me. I'll remember who didn't.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: If you're ever in Bitter Spring, look for the smoke. That'll be me or a fire, and either way you'll be useful.

lines.speaker: rufus
lines.line: I'd like it entered in the record that I jumped on purpose, Professor. It's in my contract.

lines.speaker: pett
lines.line: Rufus, you don't have a contract.

lines.speaker: rufus
lines.line: Then I'd like it entered that I should.

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: You'll be the one they talk about. I can't pay much. My husband's cattle wandered off the morning of his funeral, and I can't stop crying long enough to look for them.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: How many head?

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: Eight. Walt named every one of them. It's foolish. Bessie, Clover, the Senator... I'll stop.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Cattle don't wander on funeral mornings, Mrs. Voss. Somebody drove them.

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: Walt's partner, Lyman Gage, said he'd look in on things while we buried him. He hasn't been by since.

lines.speaker: gage
lines.line: These are my cattle, lady. Half of everything Walt had was mine.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Show me the paper.

lines.speaker: gage
lines.line: There isn't any paper. There was a handshake. Walt's dead, and handshakes die with the men who shook.

lines.speaker: gage
lines.line: She'd have sold out to the syndicate in a month anyway. I'm only taking mine before Pell takes all of it.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then you'll tell her so to her face. Walk ahead of the herd, Mr. Gage.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You stole from a widow on the morning of her husband's funeral. Draw, or don't.

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: Bessie! And the Senator! Oh, you foolish things, where have you been?

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: Lyman. Walt thought the world of you.

lines.speaker: gage
lines.line: I know it, Clem. That's the worst of it.

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: He can stay on and work it off. Walt would have wanted that, God help me. Walt was a softer fool than me.

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: You killed him. I suppose he deserved it. I don't feel any better. I thought I would.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Most people don't.

lines.speaker: clem
lines.line: Come back in the spring. There'll be calves, if the Lord's in a decent mood.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: Don't move! Oh, you moved. Never mind. You have a face for the dry plate, has anyone told you? All bones and suspicion.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've been told a lot of things about my face. That's a new one.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: Theodora Lusk, photographic artist. I need a subject in a dangerous place. Chicago won't buy a picture unless somebody might have died taking it.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: There's a ledge over Thornwood Creek where a cougar sleeps in the afternoons. I want the cat, the creek and a woman with a rifle. You.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: And if the cat wakes up?

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: Then you'll look magnificent, and I'll take two exposures.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: It's awake! It's awake and it's looking at you. Don't move, that's perfect, that's perfect!

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: I have it. I have it! The cat in the air and you not even blinking. Chicago is going to faint.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Who's the picture for, Miss Lusk?

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: A publisher. Of dime novels. He's very keen on a series: Miss Ruthie Rides Again. He knew your old show name.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: That's a name I buried in Kansas.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Print it. Give the boys in the bunkhouses something to lie about.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: You won't regret it. Well, you might. Everyone regrets dime novels eventually. But not for a year or two.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: No. Give me the plate.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: That's a week's wages and the best picture I'll ever make. Here. Break it yourself. I can't watch.

lines.speaker: theo
lines.line: For what it's worth, you'd have sold forty thousand copies. They'd have drawn your hat wrong.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: Step up, step up! The bumps of the skull are the map of the soul. A dime for your character, a dollar for your future, and for five I'll tell you why your husband left.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He didn't leave. He was shot.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: Ah. Well. The bumps were ambiguous on that point.

lines.speaker: ortiz
lines.line: He read my boy's head and said he's a natural banker. Took our seed money to invest it. We haven't seen the bank or the money.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: Slander! I'll prove my honesty the way gentlemen do. A hand of cards. You win, I return the man's money. I win, you buy a reading.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: There's a mirror in that ring, Doctor. Your hand sits over the deck like a hen on an egg.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: A family heirloom! My mother's! She was also a phrenologist.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You win a great deal for a man who reads skulls instead of cards.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: The bumps don't lie, madam. Only the people wearing them.

lines.speaker: ortiz
lines.line: Give back the seed money, or I'll show him a bump he can read with his fingers.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Give Mr. Ortiz his money. All of it. Then pick a direction and keep walking until the bumps tell you to stop.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: Mesquite Wells was such a promising crop.

lines.speaker: ortiz
lines.line: Gracias, señora. My boy will be a farmer, then. The bumps said banker, but the bumps can go to the devil.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Half your purse, Doctor. And Mr. Ortiz gets a reading that says his luck is about to change.

lines.speaker: bundy
lines.line: Madam, I've read your skull, and you have the bump of commerce. I suspected it at once.

lines.speaker: ortiz
lines.line: I trusted you, señora. That's twice this month I've been a fool.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: You're early. The comet isn't due until a quarter past two. You'll want supper. I'll want trout. There's a pool below the cabin.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I wasn't invited.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: Nobody's invited. People arrive. I've watched the sky from this rock for nineteen years, and I've learned that much about the ground.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: A good fish. You hold a rod the way you hold a rifle. Too tight, but you mean it.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: My figures say tonight. The Naval Observatory says I'm a crank who lost his post for drinking. Both are true. Only one of us is right about the comet.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: I need the lens carried up to the high rock. My knees won't do the climb any more. My heart, if I'm honest, won't do much of anything.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: Will you stay? Nobody's ever seen anything with me. It's a lonely way to be right.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll stay. I've never seen a comet. I've seen a lot of other things fall out of the sky.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: There. There. Low over the ridge, do you see the tail? Nineteen years. Nineteen years, and it came.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's beautiful.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: It is. I think I'll sit a while. Wake me when it's gone, would you? I'd hate to miss the end.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Mr. Wren? Mr. Wren. You didn't miss it. I watched it all the way down for you.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I've a long ride ahead. I hope it comes, Mr. Wren.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: It'll come. It doesn't need me to watch it. I only needed to be right.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.line: You're the woman from the dime novel. Even hermits get the mail. You were taller in the drawing.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: Ma'am! A moment of your time. Hollis Crane, Halloran National Detective Agency. There are three railroad bulls behind me who'd like to put me in the lake.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: What did you do to them?

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: I found out what they do on their days off. Get me to the ford past the marsh and I'll pay you ten dollars and owe you a favor, which is worth more, I assure you.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: You're Caddell, aren't you? The poster doesn't do you justice. Posters never do.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I hear that a great deal lately.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: Here we are. And here they are. Gentlemen, the lady.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.line: Hands where we can see them, Caddell. Two hundred dollars, and Crane gets a third for walking you in.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: A third. You came cheap, Mr. Crane.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: All right! All right. It was business. I've debts in Chicago that would turn your hair white.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: I was a real detective once. Eleven years. Then the agency let me go for drinking, and bounty work is the only kind that doesn't check references.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Then you'll have your references checked by Sheriff Mabry. Walk.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: Mabry. Of course. Pell's man. I'll be out by supper, and he'll know where you sleep.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Go back to Chicago, Mr. Crane. When I need that favor, I'll send for it.

lines.speaker: crane
lines.line: You'll have it. I'm a liar and a drunk, but I pay my debts. It's the one thing my father taught me that took.

lines.speaker: moss
lines.line: She's not going easy, Hollis! You said she'd go easy!

lines.speaker: pip
lines.line: Lantern, missus? Two cents. You're in it, page three. Not by name. A lady of uncommon aim. That's you, ain't it?

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Depends who's asking.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.line: Mick Rourke's asking, missus. Not about you. About me. I owe him for a hundred papers I couldn't sell when it rained, and he says by sundown or I'm swimming.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.line: Mr. Fenn says the stage stop at Greer's will take a whole bundle if it's there by four. I can't ride that far. You could. Fast, I mean. Real fast.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.line: Four o'clock bundle, and it's three fifty-eight. Somebody's mother raised a punctual child.

lines.speaker: agent
lines.line: Twenty past. These are yesterday's already. I'll take them at half.

lines.speaker: rourke
lines.line: Callahan! Sundown, I said, and I can see it from here.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Here's the rest of it. Count it in front of the boy, so he learns how it's done.

lines.speaker: rourke
lines.line: Pleasure. The kid's got a guardian angel with a gun. That's a first in this business.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The debt's forgiven, Mr. Rourke. You're forgiving it now.

lines.speaker: rourke
lines.line: Nobody forgives in this town, lady!

lines.speaker: pip
lines.line: You did that for me? Nobody does nothing for me. Mr. Fenn says I can sweep the press room. Real wages.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Keep your head down and your eyes open, Pip. It works for newspapers and for people.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.line: I'll put you on page one when I'm editor. By name. Spelled right, even.

lines.speaker: pip
lines.line: Don't let them get wet! Wet papers is how this whole thing started!

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: He won't trouble you again, Pip. He isn't in any condition to trouble anybody.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: Sister! You have the look of a woman who has seen what whiskey does to men. Join me. Tonight the Silver Dollar empties its barrels into the street, or I empty them myself.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: With a hatchet?

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: The Lord provides hatchets to those who ask. I asked at the hardware.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: The man who owns the Silver Dollar is Jack Bright. You'll notice the name. He was a good man before he was a saloonkeeper, and a good husband before either.

lines.speaker: jack
lines.line: Hannah. Eleven years, and you come back with a hatchet. You always did know how to make an entrance.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: And you always knew how to make an exit, Jack.

lines.speaker: bouncer
lines.line: Want me to throw her out, boss? Her and the one with the gun?

lines.speaker: jack
lines.line: I didn't leave because of the drink, Hannah. I drank because I left. I've had it backwards eleven years.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Hand me a hatchet, Mrs. Bright. Let's see what eleven years of rye looks like in the mud.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: Glory! Glory, Jack, look at it run!

lines.speaker: jack
lines.line: That was my living. Well. It was my dying too, I suppose.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Put the hatchet down. You came eleven years to swing it. Say what you came to say first.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: I came to say I hated you. I seem to have forgotten how.

lines.speaker: jack
lines.line: There's coffee in the back. Real coffee. I'll close early.

lines.speaker: hannah
lines.line: Eleven years I've told the ladies of the league that he was dead. It made a better story than the true one.

lines.speaker: jack
lines.line: Stay for the coffee, ma'am. You've earned the first cup, and I'd rather not be alone with her just yet.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Boot tracks wandering in circles, and a dragged tripod. Somebody's lost and doesn't know it yet.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: Water. Water, and please tell me which way is north. My compass swears it's under my feet.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Drink slow. North's over there, where it's always been. Who are you?

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: Linus Aldridge, assistant engineer, Meridian and Western. I was surveying a line. Then the line surveyed me.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: My transit and field book are at my camp in the slot canyon. Men came. Range detectives, they said. They took the camp and left me the desert.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: These stakes run straight through the Ybarra land and the Halvorsen south section. There's no railroad going there.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: Not a railroad. A water line. The syndicate means to pipe the deep wells to its own sections. It isn't on any map. It wasn't supposed to be on mine.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Fenn will want this, Mr. Aldridge. Your name needn't be on it.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: It will be, eventually. They'll know whose hand drew the lines. I suppose I'll go back east. I always wanted to survey something that wasn't for sale.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: The railroad will pay to have this back, and you'll keep your post. That's two things more than most people get out of the Breaks.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: Thirty dollars, they said, for the book's return. Take all of it. I don't want to look at the thing again.

lines.speaker: detective
lines.line: Somebody's in the rocks! Over by the tripod!

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: My transit! You found my transit! I'd have mourned it like a brother.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: I counted my steps to keep my wits. Eleven thousand. Then I counted them back and got nine. The desert keeps the difference.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: You walked in a circle a mile wide, Mr. Aldridge. It's a very good circle. The railroad would be proud.

lines.speaker: linus
lines.line: If you ever need a line run straight, ma'am, anywhere at all, send for me at the Meridian office. I owe you one honest survey.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: Ladies, gentlemen and loggers! Dr. Marvel's Celebrated Kestrel Elixir cures the ague, the gout, the grippe and the melancholy, and it's half price to anyone who outshoots my lovely assistant!

lines.speaker: pearl
lines.line: I've not been outshot in four counties, and I'm told I'm very lovely.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: I'll take that bet.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: Every one! Every one of them! There's only one woman alive who shoots glass like that, and she quit the ring in eighty-nine.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: Miss Ruthie. The Ozark Wonder. I barked for Colonel Brady's show the season you joined. You were sixteen and you wouldn't take a dare from anyone.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: And now you're in the dime novels! Miss Ruthie Rides Again. I've sold a hundred copies off this wagon.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Cassius Marvel. You were Cassius Mulvey then, and you sold dried peas as lucky beans.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: A man grows. Now I sell laudanum and molasses as an elixir. That's growth, of a kind.

lines.speaker: ned
lines.line: Laudanum? My brother's been drinking four bottles a week. He can't hardly swing an axe.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: It's laudanum, boys. That's why it cures the melancholy. Pour it out.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: There goes the wagon payment. Well. You always did spoil the act, Ruthie. Brady said so too.

lines.speaker: ruth
lines.line: Take the wagon and go, Cassius. And put a label on the bottles that says what's in them.

lines.speaker: marvel
lines.line: For you, Ruthie. For the old days. I'll get a printer to spell laudanum. It's a long word.

lines.speaker: pearl
lines.line: If you ever want work, the ring's still open. I'd let you win. Sometimes.

lines.speaker: pearl
lines.line: Missed a few, didn't you? Don't feel bad. Glass is honest. It's the only honest thing on this wagon.
